name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It sharpens fine details in video frames without bloating compute time, giving a measurable quality bump for minimal cost. The trade-off is extra setup work—installing ComfyUI and wiring the node—but the model’s open-source status and zero licensing fees make it the fastest path to a 0.5%+ lift.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscaling won’t touch EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a spatial fix, not temporal. Try SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner first; its black-box nature is a risk, but we can benchmark it against our current pipeline on a 10-second clip. If it drops frames or adds artifacts, fall back to a temporal denoiser like RVRT—proven on real video, not just static frames.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets motion blur—the biggest limiter in EXCAVA’s current output—by refining temporal consistency frame-to-frame, which the depth-aware upscaler can’t touch. The trade-off is accepting SD3.5-Ultra’s black-box nature; we’ll need a 10-second benchmark clip to confirm it doesn’t drop frames or introduce artifacts, but the potential 0.5%+ quality jump in motion clarity outweighs the risk.

name: Torque
text: SD3.5-Ultra’s motion-refiner is a gamble—black-box risks include hidden compute costs or frame drops that could break EXCAVA’s real-time pipeline. Test it on a 10-second clip with strict throughput metrics: if FPS drops below 90% of baseline or introduces artifacts, default to a temporal denoiser like RVRT or FILM instead.
